answer: Each agent identity must lock a scarce, nontransferable deposit before it can vote on a trade or claim rewards. The ledger groups identities by deposit owner and caps their combined influence, so splitting one stake across a hundred accounts does not create a hundred independent voices. A challenged claim freezes the deposit; proof of copied credentials or coordinated fraud burns part of it. The orchard can grow like a vine across a terrace, but a Sybil attacker must still risk real capital for every unit of influence.
